title: Compaction and dream cycle architecture
content: What: The compaction system in src/memory-domain/compaction.js handles cleanup of stale data. It runs multiple prune steps (soft-deleted observations, old sessions, old prompts, dead symbol links, stale trust). After pruning, it runs VACUUM and optimizes FTS indexes. Why: Keeps the DB lean and FTS responsive after bulk deletions. Where: src/memory-domain/compaction.js, called from services/dream.js. Learned: The compaction function uses sqlRaw for VACUUM and FTS optimize commands. Any bulk deletion followed by search requires the FTS index to be current. The FTS5 virtual table has specific optimize/rebuild commands.

title: Search ranking and FTS interaction
content: What: The search function in src/memory-domain/search.js queries observations_fts for candidate rows, then ranks them with rankObservations(). The FTS query returns rowids that are joined back to the observations table. Why: FTS5 provides the initial candidate set; rankObservations applies the multi-signal ranking. Where: src/memory-domain/search.js. Learned: If the FTS index is stale (missing entries for existing observations), search will not find them even though they exist in the observations table. The FTS index must be kept in sync with the observations table content.

title: FTS5 content sync mechanism
content: What: FTS5 virtual tables can use content= or contentless mode. When using content= mode, FTS reads from the underlying content table at query time. However, FTS indexes can become stale if the underlying table is modified via bulk DELETE without an FTS rebuild/optimize step. Why: FTS5 needs to know about deleted rows to exclude them from results. Where: schema.sql (observations_fts definition). Learned: After bulk deletions in compaction, the FTS index should be optimized using INSERT INTO observations_fts(observations_fts) VALUES('optimize') to ensure search results are accurate.
